correctness.rationale: The last-first-arrival density gives exact winner weights proportional to q_i(t); conditional nonwinning counts are independent positive-truncated Poisson, yielding the stated size-biased Poisson-binomial law. For varying Bernoulli parameter q, the likelihood ratio is increasing in a_{s-1}/a_s; log-concavity of the other independent Bernoulli sum proves this sequence is increasing, including the endpoint. All q_i(t) decrease strictly with t. Thus strict MLR, strict stochastic regression, and negative covariance for all stated integrable increasing transforms follow. The actual standalone checker passed 16,538 assertions, including an independent exact rational state recursion compared with Poissonized integration.

value.rationale: The time-conditioned singleton count is a canonical efficiency indicator for unequal coupon collection. The complete distribution and strict MLR comparison for arbitrary positive rate profiles give simultaneous control of all conditional tails and increasing losses, not merely an ordinary expected singleton count. This structural negative regression can be applied to heterogenous sampling and multi-threshold collection diagnostics.
